methods.label: Compare areas with a shared height
methods.explanation:
Triangles \(BEF\) and \(BAC\) have bases \(EF\) and \(AC\) on the same line. They share the perpendicular height from \(B\) to that line. By the formula \(\tfrac12\times\text{base}\times\text{height}\), their areas therefore have the same ratio as their bases.

Because \(E\) and \(F\) divide \(AC\) into three equal segments, \(EF=AC/3\). Thus triangle \(BEF\) has one third of the area of triangle \(BAC\). The rectangle's sides at \(B\) are perpendicular and have lengths \(5\) and \(3\), so
\[
\operatorname{Area}(BAC)=\frac12\cdot5\cdot3=\frac{15}{2}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\operatorname{Area}(BEF)
=\frac13\cdot\frac{15}{2}
=\boxed{\frac52\text{ square inches}},
\]
choice C.
methods.levelReason: The solution uses elementary triangle areas and a common-height comparison; no diagonal-length calculation is needed.
